# README.md

# Vibe Rescue: turn an unfamiliar codebase into a team handoff

English · [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) · [Full guide](docs/GUIDE.md)

By [Nguyễn Anh Nguyên](https://github.com/thusinh1969) (Nguyen Anh Nguyen) · free and open source (MIT)

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

**Vibe Rescue** gives a new team a source-linked handoff for a codebase nobody understands: what it does, how its parts connect, which request steps map to real functions, and what must be verified before a sensitive system can ship. Its first pass runs offline with no AI. Scanner findings and owner-gated repair are available when the team is ready.

## Run it in 1 minute

You need Git, Python 3.11 or newer and Bash. There is nothing to install with pip: the first `./vr` prepares its own private environment in `.venv` (about 10 seconds).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/thusinh1969/vibe_rescue.git
cd vibe_rescue
./vr doctor                               # checks your machine, says what is missing and how to fix it
./vr explore ~/path/to/your-project       # map and team handoff, no AI, a few seconds
./vr check   ~/path/to/your-project       # concrete problems with file and line, no AI
```

Then open `~/path/to/your-project/VIBE_RESCUE/START_HERE.md`: one page with what was found and which file to open next. Your project's own files are not changed, and `VIBE_RESCUE/` ignores itself in Git. The project must be a Git repository; if it is not, run `git init && git add -A && git commit -m "before rescue"` in it first.

For a plain-language AI report and fixes you approve, continue at [Step 3](#step-3-ai-report-optional) and [Step 4](#step-4-fix-with-your-approval). The longer explanations are in the [full guide](docs/GUIDE.md).

## What you get

All of it is written into `VIBE_RESCUE/` inside your project.

| file | what it is | for |
|---|---|---|
| `START_HERE.md` | one page: what was found, what to open next (English and Vietnamese) | everyone |
| `handoff.html`, `handoff.vi.html` | team handoff: purpose, functional blocks, function leads, unknowns | new teammates |
| `HANDOFF.md` | the same as text; paste it into Claude, Codex or any model | you and your AI |
| `REVIEW_WORKSHEET.md` | who proves what; reruns keep your edits | team lead |
| `architecture.html`, `source-explorer.html` | architecture map and a searchable function index | engineers |
| `atlas/INDEX.md` | maps for every language found (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, PHP, C#); `manifest.json` there says how complete they are | engineers |
| `check/findings.md` | the problem list with file, line and rule | engineers |
| `report/README.md`, `PROPOSALS.md` | the AI report in plain words, one card per problem (after Step 3) | the team |

## v0.8-preview — what is new

- **One command, a handoff the whole team can use.** The generic Atlas now writes HTML and Markdown handoffs in English and Vietnamese, plus an editable review worksheet in each language. Reruns preserve the team’s worksheet.
- **From intent to code.** The packet joins documented purpose → functional blocks → Python callsites → numbered journeys → exact function anchors. Config/prompt paths, coverage and unknowns stay visible.
- **Review work is already framed.** Agent, swarm, PII/PHI, medical and billing profiles list source leads and concrete next probes. A lead is never labelled safe or production-ready; the reviewer must run target-specific tests and traces.

![Actual v0.8-preview team handoff generated from the public synthetic support-ticket example.](docs/assets/v0.8-handoff.en.png)

[Open the complete example handoff](https://thusinh1969.github.io/vibe_rescue/examples/support_ticket/VIBE_RESCUE/handoff.html) · [Read its Markdown packet](examples/support_ticket/VIBE_RESCUE/HANDOFF.md) · [Run it on your own repo](#run-it-in-1-minute).

![The same handoff shows source-linked functional blocks, exact function leads and unknowns.](docs/assets/v0.8-blocks.en.png)

## Step by step

### Step 1: Explore (no AI)

```bash
./vr explore ~/path/to/your-project
```

Two things run. The **atlas** maps every language it finds from the Git-tracked files. The **handoff** (Python only) joins the project's own documentation to functional blocks and function names. Neither runs your code. If the map ends with "partial" (exit code 2), the map exists but some parts are missing; `atlas/manifest.json` lists which.

### Step 2: Check (no AI)

```bash
./vr check ~/path/to/your-project
```

For a Python project this runs `ruff`, `vulture`, `radon` and `bandit` (dead code, complexity, common security mistakes). Choose others with `--tools`, for example `--tools ruff,deptry,jscpd`; some need Node. The first run saves today's problems as a **baseline**, so later runs show only what is new. A tool that was skipped or failed did **not** check anything; `START_HERE.md` lists those under "NOT checked".

### Step 3: AI report (optional)

The AI explains the findings in plain words. Maps and checks need none. Pick one:

```bash
./vr ai claude                                    # A: Claude Code, with Codex as the second checker (both installed and logged in)
./vr ai openai --url https://your-server/v1 --model YOUR-WRITER-MODEL --checker-model YOUR-OTHER-MODEL    # B: any OpenAI-style server
read -rsp 'Key: ' VIBE_AGENT_API_KEY; export VIBE_AGENT_API_KEY     # B only; a local server may need no key
./vr report ~/path/to/your-project
```

Option B works with open models you host yourself and with any hosted model; use two different models for writer and checker. Only one hosted model has been tried so far, on a toy project. The AI receives your code and the findings, so use it only where you may share that code with it. Open `VIBE_RESCUE/report/README.md`, then `PROPOSALS.md`. If `./vr report` says the AI did not write the report, you got a fill-in template; run `./vr doctor`.

### Step 4: Fix with your approval

```bash
./vr fix ~/path/to/your-project --test "python -m pytest -q"
```

`--test` is a command that proves the project works today. It must pass **before** any change and must not leave new files behind (for example `__pycache__/`); add those to the project's `.gitignore`. Then: the AI writes one small plan, you approve it; a backup tag is made; the fix is made on a separate branch; your test and the checkers run again; a second AI reviews; you decide whether to merge, and `REVERT.md` gives the undo command. If nobody answers, the run stops. Nothing merges on its own.

## If something goes wrong

| you see | do this |
|---|---|
| "not a Git repository" | in the project: `git init && git add -A && git commit -m "before rescue"` |
| "Python 3.11 or newer is required" | install Python 3.11+, then run `./vr` again |
| `./vr doctor` shows MISSING | follow the line under it |
| the map is "partial" (exit code 2) | open `VIBE_RESCUE/atlas/manifest.json`; it lists what is missing, for example Node for JavaScript |
| a checker "FAILED" or "skipped" | it did not run; read `VIBE_RESCUE/logs/check.log` for the reason |
| "no AI is configured yet" | Step 3 |
| you want everything gone | in the project: `rm -rf VIBE_RESCUE .rescue .ruff_cache`; nothing else was created |

## Limits

- The map is static: it shows who can call whom, not run-time behavior. The generic handoff connects Python functions only; other languages get file-level maps.
- A finding is evidence to look at, not proof of a bug.
- A Git branch is not a security sandbox. Checkers, tests and AI programs run with your computer's permissions; use an isolated machine for code you do not trust.
- Unattended repair of production code is not approved. Repair always needs a person.

## In short (FAQ)

**What is Vibe Rescue?**
A free, MIT-licensed toolkit that turns an unfamiliar or AI-generated ("vibe-coded") Git repository into a source-linked team handoff: maps of files, functions and calls, a list of concrete problems with file and line, and, only if the owner approves, small reversible fixes.

**Is it free, and does it need an AI?**
It is free. Mapping and the handoff run offline with no AI. The AI steps (report, plan, repair) are optional and can use Claude Code, Codex, or any OpenAI-style model server, including open models you host. Only one hosted model has been tried so far, on a toy project.

**Does my code leave my machine?**
Not for mapping and checks, which run locally (third-party checking tools may be downloaded). The optional AI steps send code and findings to whichever AI you choose.

**Which languages does it support?**
Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, PHP and C#, with different levels of detail. The generic handoff connects Python functions only.

**Can it fix my code automatically?**
It prepares small fixes on a separate branch. Every plan, repair and merge needs a human yes, and a file tells you how to undo it. Unattended repair of production code is not approved.

**How is it different from paid vibe-code rescue services?**
Those are done-for-you human services. Vibe Rescue is a free tool you run yourself, with evidence you can check. It does not replace an engineer's judgment.

## Status and license

**v0.8-preview** creates a source-linked team handoff from any approved repo scope, with a review worksheet to collect owners and exact-build receipts. The [preview contract](docs/V0.8_PREVIEW.md) explains what the generic Atlas proves and what remains a reviewer task. A detailed control review is written by a human reviewer; the tool does not generate an equivalent safety verdict for every team. Repair still requires owner approval and has [open safety gaps](STATUS.md#current-preview-gaps). Package tooling may normalize `0.8.0-preview` to `0.8.0rc0`.

License: [MIT](LICENSE).

# docs/GUIDE.md

# Vibe Rescue: the full guide

The short, step-by-step README is [README.md](../README.md). This guide keeps the longer explanations.

# Vibe Rescue: turn an unfamiliar codebase into a team handoff

English · [Tiếng Việt](GUIDE.vi.md) · [Back to the short README](../README.md)

By [Nguyễn Anh Nguyên](https://github.com/thusinh1969) (Nguyen Anh Nguyen) · free and open source (MIT)

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

**Vibe Rescue** gives a new team a source-linked handoff for a codebase nobody understands: what it does, how its parts connect, which request steps map to real functions, and what must be verified before a sensitive system can ship. Its first pass runs offline with no AI. Scanner findings and owner-gated repair are available when the team is ready.

## v0.8-preview — what is new

- **One command, a handoff the whole team can use.** The generic Atlas now writes HTML and Markdown handoffs in English and Vietnamese, plus an editable review worksheet in each language. Reruns preserve the team’s worksheet.
- **From intent to code.** The packet joins documented purpose → functional blocks → Python callsites → numbered journeys → exact function anchors. Config/prompt paths, coverage and unknowns stay visible.
- **Review work is already framed.** Agent, swarm, PII/PHI, medical and billing profiles list source leads and concrete next probes. A lead is never labelled safe or production-ready; the reviewer must run target-specific tests and traces.

![Actual v0.8-preview team handoff generated from the public synthetic support-ticket example.](assets/v0.8-handoff.en.png)

[Open the complete example handoff](https://thusinh1969.github.io/vibe_rescue/examples/support_ticket/VIBE_RESCUE/handoff.html) · [Read its Markdown packet](../examples/support_ticket/VIBE_RESCUE/HANDOFF.md) · [Run it on your own repo](#quick-start).

![The same handoff shows source-linked functional blocks, exact function leads and unknowns.](assets/v0.8-blocks.en.png)

Good for: inheriting a legacy project, cleaning up "vibe-coded" or AI-generated code, auditing technical debt, and onboarding a new developer. It works on any Git project and maps Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, PHP and C#. Mapping and checking use free tools and need **no paid AI**.

It does two jobs:

1. **EXPLORE.** It reads the project and shows your team what is really in it: which parts exist, what starts the program, which files are huge, who depends on whom, and which parts nobody understands.
2. **FIX.** It checks for potential problems (dead code, copy-paste, over-complicated files, tangled dependencies, leaked passwords, outdated libraries), explains findings with their file and line, and, only if you approve, prepares small fixes that can be undone.

> **Source fixes require your approval.** EXPLORE writes reports, and third-party checkers may create caches. Every repair needs your approval and can be reverted.

## The problem it solves

A team that builds fast ("vibe coding", with people or AI) ends up with a project like this:

- Nobody can say how the parts fit together.
- Files with thousands of lines that do ten different jobs.
- The same code copied in five places.
- Code and libraries that nobody uses any more but nobody dares to delete.
- Two rule files that say opposite things.
- Fear: "if I fix this, three other things will break".

Vibe Rescue turns that fog into **a list of concrete, checkable facts** and **a safe path to fix them**.

## Job 1: EXPLORE (what you learn)

| Question your team asks | What Vibe Rescue gives you |
| --- | --- |
| "What is in this project?" | Languages used, what starts the program (entry points), how tests run, the 10 largest files, which files look generated or copied from elsewhere. |
| "Who calls whom?" | Searchable HTML and SVG pages for tracked source files, statically resolved symbols and calls. Large Python diagrams are split into linked SVG pages; cross-page calls remain in the HTML catalog. Unresolved calls are marked. Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, PHP and C# have [different levels of detail](LOGIC_ATLAS.md). |
| "Which parts are tangled?" | Files that import each other in circles, files everyone depends on, and the largest files. |
| "What do we not understand?" | A list of **unknowns**. The tool writes "I don't know" instead of guessing. |
| "Where was the code rushed?" | Which files were rewritten the most in the Git history. |
| "What AI rules and tools are lying around?" | An inventory of rule files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, ...) and which ones are unused, outdated, duplicated or contradict each other. |

![English Source Atlas: how the work flows, what is checked, what can fail, and where the risks are.](assets/source-atlas-preview.en.png)

[Open this project's own Source Atlas](https://thusinh1969.github.io/vibe_rescue/docs/assets/repo-explorer.en.html) to see what such a map looks like. The picture above is a screenshot of that page.

## Job 2: FIX (what it looks for)

Free, well-known checking tools search the code. Every result is saved with its file and line. Nothing is "a feeling".

| Problem in plain words | How it is found |
| --- | --- |
| **Dead code**: functions and files nobody calls | `vulture` (Python), `knip` (JavaScript/TypeScript) |
| **Over-complicated functions**: too many branches to understand | `radon`, `ruff` |
| **Copy-paste**: the same block in several places | `jscpd` |
| **Tangled structure**: files importing each other in circles, one file everyone needs | built-in import-graph check, `dependency-cruiser`, `import-linter` |
| **Unused or missing libraries** | `deptry` |
| **Security mistakes**: passwords in code, `eval`, running shell commands unsafely, unsafe file extraction | `bandit`, `semgrep` with rules in `tools/rules/` |
| **Leaked secrets** and **libraries with known holes** | `gitleaks`, `trivy`, `osv-scanner` (downloaded by the optional installer) |
| **Broken links and messy docs** | `lychee`, `markdownlint` |
| **Personal data** such as Vietnamese phone and ID numbers in code | custom rules in `tools/rules/` |

The first run saves **a snapshot of today's problems** (called a "baseline"). Every later run tells you only what is **new**, so the team can pay off old problems step by step instead of facing a wall of red.

Tools that are not installed are reported as `skipped` or `failed`. That means **not checked**; it never means "no problems".

## Who does what: machines, AI, you

| Who | What they do | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Machines** (the checking tools above) | Find problems and record file, line and evidence. | They are exact and repeatable. They do not guess. |
| **AI, writer** | Reads the machine results, explains each problem in plain words, writes a small plan, and makes the fix on a separate branch. | The machines find problems but cannot explain them or write code. The AI can. It is only allowed to use findings the machines recorded. |
| **AI, checker** | Re-runs everything and reads the change as a second pair of eyes. | An AI that checks its own work misses its own mistakes. A second model, different from the first, is a real second opinion. |
| **You** | Approve the plan, approve the repair, decide the merge. | You know your business. Silence is never a "yes": if nobody answers in time, the run stops. |

## Which AI do I need? You choose, any budget

**EXPLORE needs no AI.** For FIX, the AI reads machine results, explains them, writes one small plan and checks a change. The harness supports separate writer and checker models; their reliability depends on the models and the project.

| Your situation | Suggested models (maintainer's guidance, not measured by this repository) |
| --- | --- |
| Free or very cheap: run on your own machine or a cheap server | **Gemma-4-31B** and **Qwen 3.8 27B**: one writes, the other checks |
| Want stronger, still cheap | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Haiku, GPT Luna 6 |
| Large or very tangled project | Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8 Max, GLM 5.3 |

The design goal is **any server that speaks the common OpenAI-style `/v1/chat/completions` format**, so you can swap models without changing anything else. Use two *different* models for writer and checker; the point is that the checker is not the writer. "Open-weight" simply means models whose files you can download and run yourself, which is the cheapest option and keeps your code on your own machine.

**What works today, honestly:**

- Steps 1 and 2 (explore and find problems) need **no AI at all**.
- The AI steps (report, plan, repair, second check) can run through either:
  - **Claude Code and Codex**, command-line agent programs (paid; the default in `config.toml`), or
  - the built-in adapter `scripts/openai_agent.py` for **any OpenAI-style server**: set `cli = "openai"`, the model id and `--base-url` (see step 3, option B). The adapter gives the model read-only tools and lets it write only where each step allows. It cannot run commands; Vibe Rescue itself runs the tests, scanners and scope checks.
- **Tested so far:** automatic tests with a scripted fake server (what may be read and written, secrets hidden, failures), and **one full FIX run on a tiny made-up project with one hosted model** (`deepseek-flash`): report, plan, your approvals, a one-line fix, the second check, merge and the undo file all worked. **Not tested yet:** Gemma or Qwen on a real server, or the full FIX workflow on a real project. One run is an observation, not a statistic.
- Weaker models can write a plan that fails the plan check or a fix that the second check rejects. Then the tool **stops and changes nothing**; that is the safety net working, not a crash.
- A separate sample-task test (`scripts/model_rescue_eval.py`, last section) grades a model on made-up tasks. Only `deepseek-flash` has recorded results (map 4 of 4, plan 4 of 4, review 3 of 4, or 4 of 4 after fixing a slip in the grader); for Gemma and Qwen the test exists but no results are recorded.

## Quick start

You need **Git**, **Python 3.11 or newer** (with `venv` and `pip`) and **Bash**. The optional downloaded checking tools are pinned for Linux x86-64 only.

### Step 1: your first map (5 minutes, no AI, no account)

Copy this single line into a terminal. It downloads the tool, sets it up in its own folder, and makes a first inventory of Vibe Rescue itself:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/thusinh1969/vibe_rescue.git && cd vibe_rescue && python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && python -m pip install uv tree-sitter-language-pack==0.13.0 && python scripts/logic_atlas.py --target . --inventory-only --outdir reports/first-look
```

Open `reports/first-look/INDEX.md`. If you open a new terminal later, switch the tool back on first: `cd vibe_rescue && . .venv/bin/activate`.

Now map **your** project:

```bash
python scripts/logic_atlas.py --target /path/to/your/project --outdir reports/atlas
```

Open `reports/atlas/INDEX.md` and follow the links.

- Python projects produce `python-map.html`, one or more linked `python-map*.svg` pages, and `python-calls.dot`.
- JavaScript/TypeScript projects produce `frontend-map.html` and `frontend-functions.html` (needs Node and `npx`).
- Add `--pdf` for a PDF if a PDF renderer is installed.
- Only files tracked by Git are read.
- Exit code `2` with the word `INCOMPLETE` means the map exists but some parts are missing. Open `manifest.json` in the same folder to see which.
- Large Python scopes are split into shard maps automatically; open `python-shards/INDEX.md`. Calls across shards are unresolved. Use `--scope path/to/folder` for a focused journey.

For an **architecture-first** map of why blocks exist, how approved documentation describes the journey, and which Python calls/imports connect those blocks, run:

```bash
python scripts/repo_explorer.py --generic --root /path/to/your/project --sources src tests --out reports/source-explorer.html
```

Open `reports/handoff.html` first for the team-facing packet; share `reports/HANDOFF.md` in a review or issue. Assign proof owners in `reports/REVIEW_WORKSHEET.md`; reruns preserve that file. English and Vietnamese versions are generated together. Follow its links to `reports/architecture.html` for blocks, callsites and SVG, then `reports/source-explorer.html` for Python parameters, guards, raises, callers and callees. Both maps have adjacent JSON. Replace `src tests` with your approved source directories. The generic map inventories non-Python files; detailed function calls currently require Python.

The tool reads a bounded set of README/DESIGN/ARCHITECTURE/PIPELINE Markdown files within those source directories and the root README. Add `--docs path/to/your/design.md` for another approved document. Add `--profile agent`, `--profile swarm`, `--profile pii`, `--profile medical` or `--profile billing` to show a relevant control checklist. A matching function name or test is only a **lead**; the HTML keeps runtime safety and production readiness unverified until your team runs traces and fault tests. The generator does not execute the target or call an LLM. See the [public workflow diagram](assets/vibe-rescue-v1-architecture.html) for how exploration feeds the repair gates.

### Step 2: find the problems (no AI)

For a Python project:

```bash
python scripts/rescue_voyage.py --path /path/to/your/project --stages map,prove --tools ruff
```

`--tools ruff` runs one checker. Leave `--tools` out to run every checker that is available.

Read:

- `<your project>/.rescue/voyage/prove/findings.md`: the problem list.
- `<your project>/.rescue/voyage/prove/run.summary.json`: what ran and what did not.

Everything is written into the hidden folder `.rescue/` of your project. Add `.rescue/` to that project's `.gitignore` so it is not committed by accident. For code you do not trust, work inside a throwaway virtual machine or container, because checking tools may run the project's own settings (see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)).

If your project contains private data or directories that must not be read, do not run `rescue_voyage.py` on its root: its MAP stage inspects the whole target. Use `logic_atlas.py --scope path/to/approved/code` and `fanout.py --target /path/to/approved/subdirectory --tools ruff --outdir reports/scan` instead; review those outputs before sharing them.

### Step 3: get the report in plain words (needs an AI)

Choose one option. If you use no AI, steps 1 and 2 already give you a lot. See also [Which AI do I need?](#which-ai-do-i-need-you-choose-any-budget).

**Option A: Claude Code and Codex** (paid, command-line programs). Install and log in once:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code @openai/codex
claude auth login
codex login
cp config.toml config.local.toml
```

Open `config.local.toml`. It says which program plays which role (leave `model` empty to use each program's default):

```toml
[roles.write]  # writes the plan and the fix
cli = "claude"
model = ""
extra_args = []

[roles.audit]  # writes the report
cli = "claude"
model = ""
extra_args = []

[roles.verify]  # second, independent reviewer of the fix
cli = "codex"
model = ""
extra_args = []
```

**Option B: any OpenAI-style server** (open models you host, or any cheap or strong hosted model). Put this in `config.local.toml`, with the exact model id your server reports at `/v1/models`. Use a *different* model for `verify` than for `write` and `audit`:

```toml
[roles.write]
cli = "openai"
model = "your-writer-model-id"
extra_args = ["--base-url", "https://your-server.example/v1"]

[roles.audit]
cli = "openai"
model = "your-writer-model-id"
extra_args = ["--base-url", "https://your-server.example/v1"]

[roles.verify]
cli = "openai"
model = "your-checker-model-id"
extra_args = ["--base-url", "https://your-server.example/v1", "--api-key-env", "VIBE_CHECKER_API_KEY"]
```

Type the key into your terminal only (never into a file): `read -rsp 'Key: ' VIBE_AGENT_API_KEY; export VIBE_AGENT_API_KEY`. A local server that needs no key can leave it empty. Plain `http://` is accepted on your own machine (`localhost`); for any other host use `https://`, or add `--allow-http` only for a private server you trust.

> **Privacy:** the report, plan and fix steps send your code and findings to the server you chose (the company behind Claude Code or Codex, or your own server in option B). Use them only if you are allowed to share that code with it.

Run:

```bash
VIBE_LLM_CONFIG="$PWD/config.local.toml" python scripts/rescue_voyage.py \
  --path /path/to/your/project --stages map,prove,review --tools ruff
```

You get a small folder, `<your project>/.rescue/voyage/review/`:

| File | For | Contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `README.md` | the whole team, 2 minutes | What is good, what to fix first (top 5 to 7), where each number came from. |
| `PROPOSALS.md` | engineers | One card per problem: the problem in plain words, the evidence (file and line), how to fix it step by step, the risk, how to verify, priority. |
| `EVIDENCE/` | whoever wants to check | The raw machine results, a table that marks every number the AI quoted as matching, mismatching or not checkable, and a second AI's cross-check. |

Look for `agent_wrote=True` in the console. If it says `False`, the AI did not run and you received a fill-in template built from the machine results.

An example card (made-up values, only to show the shape):

```text
P-03  Payment code is copied into three files
Evidence:  billing/a.py:40-95, billing/b.py:12-67, billing/c.py:30-85 (copy-paste check)
Fix:       1. Move the shared block into billing/common.py  2. Call it from the three files
Risk:      Medium. All three files handle money.
Verify:    python3 -m pytest tests/billing -q
Not doing: changing any prices or rules
```

### Step 4: fix, with your approval

First choose a **safety command**: a command that proves your project still works today, such as its tests. It must pass **before** any change, and it must **not leave new files behind** (for example Python's `__pycache__/`): add them to `.gitignore`, or the fix is rejected as touching files outside the plan.

```bash
VIBE_LLM_CONFIG="$PWD/config.local.toml" python scripts/rescue_voyage.py \
  --path /path/to/your/project --stages map,prove,review,plan --tools ruff \
  --probe "python3 -m pytest -q" --owner interactive
```

The AI writes **one small plan with one goal**. The tool checks the plan is complete (what files may change, what must not change, a check after each step, when to stop, how to undo). It then prints the plan and asks you in the terminal. Read `<your project>/.rescue/voyage/PLAN-001.md` before you answer. Your approval is tied to the exact text of the plan and the exact version of your project: change either and you must approve again.

If you stop here, nothing in your project has changed. Adding the stage `repair` makes the tool ask for two more "yes" answers (to start, and to merge). The full protocol is in [docs/VOYAGE.md](VOYAGE.md).

## How a fix stays safe

1. A backup tag is put on your project before anything changes.
2. The fix is made on a separate branch in a separate folder, never on your main branch.
3. The AI may only touch the files named in the approved plan. It may not add libraries, change public interfaces, or edit tests just to make them pass.
4. Your safety command runs before and after. If the results differ, the fix is dropped.
5. The checking tools run again. Any **new** problem blocks the fix.
6. The second AI re-runs everything and reads the change. Only "approve" moves on.
7. **You** decide whether to merge. After a merge, `REVERT.md` gives the exact command to undo it.

## Questions and fixes

**What is the difference between EXPLORE and FIX?**
EXPLORE (steps 1 and 2) maps and checks code without intentionally changing source; it writes evidence and third-party checkers may create caches. FIX (steps 3 and 4) adds an AI that explains, plans and repairs, always with your approval.

**Do I need an expensive AI?**
No. The checking tools produce findings; the AI explains, plans and checks. There is not yet evidence that two small models are reliable for every project. See [Which AI do I need?](#which-ai-do-i-need-you-choose-any-budget). Without any AI you still get steps 1 and 2.

**Can I use Gemma or Qwen on my real project?**
The connection exists (option B in step 3), but it has only been tried with a hosted model on a toy project, not yet with Gemma or Qwen. Try it first on a small project or a copy, and run the sample-task test (last section) to see how your model does.

**It says `INCOMPLETE` or exit code 2.**
The map is partial. Read `manifest.json` in the output folder. Typical causes: Node or `npx` is missing (JavaScript/TypeScript), or some imports could not be resolved.

**A tool shows `skipped` or `failed`.**
That part was not checked. Install what the message names, or accept the gap and write it down.

**`agent_wrote=False`.**
The AI program did not run. Check that `claude` or `codex` is installed and that you are logged in, then run the same command again.

**Will it change my project while exploring or checking?**
Vibe Rescue itself only writes into `.rescue/`. Third-party checking tools may create their own cache files, so use a copy of your project if that matters.

**Is the map the truth?**
No. It is read from the code without running it. It shows who *can* call whom, not what happens at run time, and it marks what it could not resolve as `unknown`. To record real paths, use [docs/JOURNEY_TEMPLATE.md](JOURNEY_TEMPLATE.md) and prove them with tests.

## Test any model on sample tasks (works today)

This works with any OpenAI-style server, including open models you run yourself. It sends only made-up code, never your project. Use the exact model name your server reports at `/v1/models`:

```bash
export VIBE_EVAL_BASE_URL="https://your-server.example/v1"
export VIBE_EVAL_MODEL="google/gemma-4-31B-it"
read -rsp 'Server API key: ' VIBE_EVAL_API_KEY; export VIBE_EVAL_API_KEY; printf '\n'
python scripts/model_rescue_eval.py --out reports/model-eval/gemma.json
```

For Qwen, change the model name to the one your server shows and use a different output file. Add `--allow-http` only for a private server you trust. Results and limits: [docs/SMALL_MODEL_EVAL.md](SMALL_MODEL_EVAL.md).

## Limits you should know

- The map is **static**: it is read from the code, not from a running program. It cannot see a button click turning into a web request unless you document that path.
- Checking tools find signals, not verdicts. A finding is evidence to look at, not proof of a bug.
- A Git branch is **not** a security sandbox. Checkers, tests and AI programs run with your computer's permissions. Use an isolated machine for code you do not trust.
- Hiding secrets in reports is best effort. Review `.rescue/`, `reports/` and `logs_audit/` before sharing them.
- Unattended repair of production code is **not approved**. Repair always needs a person.

## Words used here

| Word | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Finding** | A problem reported by a checking tool, with file and line. |
| **Baseline** | The snapshot of today's problems, saved so later runs show only what is new. |
| **Safety command** ("probe") | A command, such as your tests, that must give the same result before and after a fix. |
| **Owner** | The human who says yes or no. |
| **Branch** | A separate copy of the change; your main code is untouched until you merge. |

## What is in this folder

| Folder or file | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/` | The commands you run (`logic_atlas.py`, `rescue_voyage.py`, ...). |
| `agents/` | Written instructions for each AI role (auditors, planner, fixer, reviewer). |
| `tools/` | Which checking tools and versions are used (`tools/manifest.toml`), and the custom rules. |
| `config.toml` | Which AI program plays which role. Copy it to `config.local.toml` to change it. |
| `targets/registry.toml` | An optional address book of projects you rescue often. |
| `docs/` | Detailed documents (mostly in Vietnamese). |
| `tests/` | Automatic tests of Vibe Rescue itself. |

## In short (FAQ)

**What is Vibe Rescue?**
A free, MIT-licensed toolkit that turns an unfamiliar or AI-generated ("vibe-coded") Git repository into a source-linked team handoff: maps of files, functions and calls, a list of concrete problems with file and line, and, only if the owner approves, small reversible fixes.

**Is it free, and does it need an AI?**
It is free. Mapping and the handoff run offline with no AI. The AI steps (report, plan, repair) are optional and can use Claude Code, Codex, or any OpenAI-style model server, including open models you host. Only one hosted model has been tried so far, on a toy project.

**Does my code leave my machine?**
Not for mapping and checks, which run locally (third-party checking tools may be downloaded). The optional AI steps send code and findings to whichever AI you choose.

**Which languages does it support?**
Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, PHP and C#, with different levels of detail. The generic handoff connects Python functions only.

**Can it fix my code automatically?**
It prepares small fixes on a separate branch. Every plan, repair and merge needs a human yes, and a file tells you how to undo it. Unattended repair of production code is not approved.

**How is it different from paid vibe-code rescue services?**
Those are done-for-you human services. Vibe Rescue is a free tool you run yourself, with evidence you can check. It does not replace an engineer's judgment.

## Status and license

**v0.8-preview** creates a source-linked team handoff from any approved repo scope, with a review worksheet to collect owners and exact-build receipts. The [preview contract](V0.8_PREVIEW.md) explains what the generic Atlas proves and what remains a reviewer task. A detailed control review is written by a human reviewer; the tool does not generate an equivalent safety verdict for every team. Repair still requires owner approval and has [open safety gaps](../STATUS.md#current-preview-gaps). Package tooling may normalize `0.8.0-preview` to `0.8.0rc0`.

# docs/V0.8_PREVIEW.md

# v0.8-preview — capability contract

[Tiếng Việt](V0.8_PREVIEW.vi.md) · Package metadata: `0.8.0-preview`
(packaging tools may normalize it to `0.8.0rc0`). This is a **preview of the
generic workflow**, not a certification for every repository. Install from the
source checkout as shown in the README; a Python wheel is not supported yet.

## What another team can run today

```bash
python scripts/repo_explorer.py --generic \
  --root /path/to/project --sources src tests \
  --profile agent --profile pii \
  --out /path/to/project/VIBE_RESCUE/source-explorer.html
```

Choose only approved source directories. The command runs offline and writes
EN/VI `handoff.html` + `HANDOFF.md` packets, `REVIEW_WORKSHEET.md` in both
languages, `architecture.html/.json`, and
`source-explorer.html/.json` together. Start with the handoff; its source links
lead into the Atlas and function explorer. The architecture page connects
bounded documentation claims to directory blocks, Python
source-level calls/imports, exact backtick step anchors, config/prompt *paths*,
control candidates and explicit unknowns. The second page lets engineers inspect
Python parameters, callers/callees, guards and raises. Other supported languages
enter the file inventory; this generic command does not connect their functions
to Python or to UI/HTTP routes. The separate `logic_atlas.py` has language-specific
maps with the limits described in [LOGIC_ATLAS.md](LOGIC_ATLAS.md).

`rescue_voyage.py --path /path/to/project --stages map,prove,review` can run the
scanner and agent-review workflow on a chosen target when its source and provider
policy permit it. Unlike the scoped Atlas, MAP inspects the target root. Plan,
repair and merge need owner decisions; worktrees and diff checks do not sandbox
agent/scanner processes. See [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) and the
[owner pact](OWNER_PACT.md) before using FIX on a real project.

## What the output proves

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

| Output | Evidence level | Reviewer still needs to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Handoff block, journey and control card | Static source/documentation evidence | Assign a reviewer and collect target-specific proof; the packet is not a safety verdict. |
| Function, call/import, file and line | Static source observation | Check dynamic dispatch and trace the served path. |
| Purpose or journey step from docs | Documented claim | Check that the document matches the current code. |
| Exact function ID in backticks | Exact source binding | Verify the step actually executes for the target scenario. |
| Harness, PII/PHI, medical, billing or swarm card | Candidate or not located in scope | Trace intake, authority, egress, final output and failures; collect redacted receipts. |
| Scanner or model review | Finding or hypothesis | Reproduce, assess impact, review proposed fix and run target tests. |

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD013 -->

A detailed control review is written by an independent human reviewer after
following code paths and focused tests. Vibe
Rescue now generates the **starting handoff for any approved scope**, with
specific source links and probes. It does not automatically reproduce that
reviewer's runtime or clinical conclusions. A green unit test or a function
named `mask` cannot establish safety or production readiness.

## Preview evidence and remaining gates

- On the public synthetic [support-ticket example](../examples/support_ticket/),
  the same generic command mapped 6 code files, 6 blocks, 8 static relations
  and 5/5 explicitly named journey functions; its EN/VI handoffs and preserved
  review worksheets are checked in. A fixture keeps unknown function IDs
  unknown. This tests portability of EXPLORE, not a live full-stack request or
  FIX.
- The [Architecture Atlas contract](ARCHITECTURE_ATLAS.md) documents evidence
  states, scope exclusions and current parser limits. The long-term
  [product objective](PRODUCT_NORTH_STAR.md) and [V1.0 plan](../PLAN.md) remain
  active; `v0.8-preview` does not close their control or release gates.
- A wheel build currently fails at setuptools' ambiguous flat-layout package
  discovery. The source-checkout commands above work; do not advertise
  `pip install vibe-rescue` until distribution layout and installed entry
  points are designed and tested.
- Before claiming a target is production-ready, its team must independently
  validate the exact build and active configuration with UAT/production traces,
  failure injection, security review and domain-specific test cases. Sensitive
  artifacts stay in that team's controlled workspace.

# SECURITY.md (English)

## English

Git worktrees separate candidate changes; they are **not security sandboxes**.
Scanners, probes, third-party tools and agent CLIs may execute target code or
send data over the network. Redaction is best effort. Use an isolated environment
for untrusted repositories, review artifacts before sharing, and audit Git history
before publishing.
